import ssl, threading, socketserver, http.server, sys
import requests, requests.adapters as A
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.poolmanager import PoolManager
print("requests from", requests.__file__)
seen = []
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        cert = self.connection.getpeercert()
        seen.append(dict(x[0] for x in cert["subject"])["commonName"] if cert else None)
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Length","2"); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b"ok")
    def log_message(self,*a): pass
def serve():
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
    ctx.load_cert_chain("srv.pem","srv.key")
    ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_OPTIONAL
    ctx.load_verify_locations("cli.pem")
    srv = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1",0),H)
    srv.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(srv.socket, server_side=True)
    threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever,daemon=True).start()
    return srv.server_address[1]
port = serve()
url = f"https://localhost:{port}/"
# trust the test server via the shared preloaded context (stand-in for a publicly-trusted server)
A._preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations("srv.pem")

print("--- Exp1: request WITH client cert, then request WITHOUT (verify=True both, separate Sessions)")
requests.get(url, cert=("cli.pem","cli.key"))
requests.get(url)
print("server saw client cert CN for req1, req2:", seen)

print("--- Exp2: user-supplied ssl_context on adapter honored with default verify=True?")
seen.clear()
class Ad(HTTPAdapter):
    def init_poolmanager(self, connections, maxsize, block=False, **kw):
        c = ssl.create_default_context(); c.load_verify_locations("srv.pem")
        c.load_cert_chain("cli.pem","cli.key")   # user's own client identity
        self.user_ctx = c
        self.poolmanager = PoolManager(num_pools=connections, maxsize=maxsize, block=block, ssl_context=c)
s = requests.Session(); ad = Ad(); s.mount("https://", ad)
# fresh module context lacking client cert: use a new interpreter state by comparing contexts used
r = s.get(url)
pool = ad.poolmanager.connection_from_host("localhost", port, "https", pool_kwargs=A._urllib3_request_context(requests.Request("GET",url).prepare(), True, None)[1])
print("pool ssl_context is user's:", pool.conn_kw.get("ssl_context") is ad.user_ctx, "| is module preloaded:", pool.conn_kw.get("ssl_context") is A._preloaded_ssl_context)
EOF
